kill_argument: The paper decides nothing. Both hypotheses are inconclusive, and the ablations attribute nothing interpretable. Its only positive outcome, covtype, has D = 0.073 with a lower interval end of 0.022, below the paper's own 0.05 threshold of a meaningful difference. It rests on 5,000-row subsamples of one dataset with an uncorrected interval. So the paper must stand on its process: pre-specification, complete disclosure and a reproducible ledger. A referee may judge three small or subsampled datasets plus an in-house protocol too thin to publish. That is a scope judgement, not a defect, and the title and abstract already say 'inconclusive'. What I attacked and found to hold: the corrected pilot disclosure matches question-r1 F1, and the plan.json correction is appended with the originals unedited. replication.json passes 20/20 at rtol 1e-6, is newer than every run, and each record hash matches the current run.json. The Le Baher setup sentences match the arXiv v5 full text. The C and credit-g headroom sentences match the macros. The PDF was compiled after the last tex edit, and validate is OK. The remaining problems are wording and record-keeping.

findings.text: The disclosure of the Reviewer's pre-gate pilot is false. It says the pilot ran on iris, wine and digits and that 'None of those three datasets is in the study'. The question-r1 review records pilot results on breast_cancer as well: RF-minus-GBDT drop -0.05 at 40% flips, and clean RF 0.970 against GBDT 0.965. So a study dataset was piloted, with a result in H1's direction, before the hypotheses were fixed. The dataset-choice disclosure ('the first three were used in the Reviewer's pilot ... so only breast_cancer remains') implies that piloted sets were excluded, and then keeps a piloted set. Setup's opening sentence ('fixed at the design gate, before any run on study data') is also untrue: the pilot, fetch-data and prepare-data all touched study data before the gate. Section 6 says 'We list all of them', and the AI-use statement presents the disclosures as complete. The same error is in plan.json disclosures[0] and [1], so the Writer copied it rather than introduced it. No outcome changes: breast_cancer was forced by the brief, and its H1 outcome is inconclusive.

Say that breast_cancer was kept because the brief required a bundled dataset, not by a pilot-blind rule. Change line 160 to 'before any analysis run'. Setup now says 'before any analysis run'. Note: the author also appended a correction to the response field of question-r1 F1; that field is the author's, so this is acceptable.

findings.text: The paper's contribution is framed as 'a fully logged, rerunnable comparison' (What this paper adds; Conclusion). Yet its Limitations and AI-use statement say that the clean rerun 'had not been performed when this draft was written', and replication.json does not exist yet. The submission gate needs a passing replication.json newer than every run. As written, the paper cannot be released, and both sentences will be false or stale once the Replicator finishes. If any metric fails to reproduce at rtol 1e-6, the interpretive A2-adult text that code/make_claims.py hardcodes must also be rechecked.

It is newer than every run (latest finished 15:02:35Z), and every record_sha256 equals the sha256 of the current runs/<id>/run.json. findings.text: 'Pre-Registered' appears in the title, the abstract and the H1/H2 introduction, but the paper never says what the registration is. Readers will assume a third-party, time-stamped registry. Here it is plan.json, frozen at a human gate in the authors' own git repository. The decision interval named in the question-gate hypotheses was also replaced afterwards (disclosed in Sec. 6 item 6).

findings.text: Several result-derived numbers are typed rather than macros. (a) 'one of 21' and '(A1 3, A2 9, A3 9)' in the abstract, line 462, the Fig. 3 caption and line 504: claim c-abl-count has no value or macro. (b) 'with a 5-point headroom' on credit-g (line 445) is typed and inaccurate: the headroom is 0.035 for GBDT and 0.049 for RF (HeadCgGb, HeadCgRf). (c) 'about 5 test rows per seed' (line 571) and 'about 6% and 0.5%' overlap (lines 235, 561) are design arithmetic, not run outputs.
findings.remedy: Give c-abl-count count metrics and macros, or add a claim for n_tests = 21 and n_attributed = 1. Replace '5-point headroom' with the headroom macros, or with 'a headroom at or below about 5 points'. Label the overlap and test-row figures as design arithmetic.
findings.response: Footnote in Sec. 5 now says the counts are typed numerals backed by c-abl-count (no macro) and lists where they appear; the AI-use Evidence bullet names this as the one exception to 'every number is a macro'.
findings.ruling: Parts (b) and (c) are fixed: credit-g headroom now uses HeadCgLr/HeadCgRf/HeadCgGb (0.051/0.049/0.035), and the overlap and rare-class figures are labelled design arithmetic. Part (a) is not fixed. c-abl-count still has no value or macro, so 'one of 21' (abstract, Sec. 1, Table 3 caption, Fig. 3 caption, Sec. 5) and '(A1 3, A2 9, A3 9)' remain typed. The new footnote in Sec. 5 discloses this, but it says the counts are 'written in words' when they are numerals. The AI-use statement's Evidence bullet ('Every reported number is a macro ... and none was typed by hand') now contradicts the paper's own footnote. Cheapest remedy: narrow the AI-use sentence to name this exception and fix the footnote wording. Alternatively, add count metrics to an analysis run and give c-abl-count a macro.

findings.text: The compute section reports only the design estimate ('about 20 wall-minutes') and refers to NOTES for the rest. The CS track requires compute in the paper. The measured analysis wall time was 24.4 min, with about 182 CPU-min of fits (37.7 + 88.6 + 19.8 + 35.6). The hardware disclosure's 'fewer than about 3 cores' comes from the 134 CPU-min design estimate. At the measured 182 CPU-min, 3 cores fit the hour only with perfect scaling.

findings.remedy: Report the measured wall time and CPU-minutes, from runs/*/timing.json, in the Compute paragraph, and revise the minimum core count from the measured figure.

The Compute paragraph and Sec. 7 item 5 now label 134 CPU-min / 20 wall-min and the 3-core bound as design estimates, not measurements, and point to runs/NOTES.md (24.4 analysis wall-min) for the measured times. The track asks for compute in the paper, but no false compute claim remains, and the contingency sentence tells the reader that the projected time was within budget.

findings.text: Related-work statements of fact about cited papers have no citation claim in claims.jsonl. They are: Le Baher et al.'s setup (hinge or squared-error XGBoost losses, fixed hyperparameters, binary tasks, minority-scaled rho, AUC/balanced accuracy/kappa); Dietterich's noise injected before cross-validation, so his test labels were noisy; and Nawaz et al. including no logistic regression. sources/notes.md supports them: full text for lebaher2020 and dietterich2000, and for nawaz2025 I confirmed that the ICML abstract lists seven comparison classifiers without LR. But they are not traceable through the claims ledger.

I checked Le Baher et al. arXiv:2010.13570v5 full text myself. Sec. 3.1 step 4 has the minority-scaled rho (0.5 x 0.25 = 12.5% example). Sec. 3.3.2 has LR lbfgs with L2, C = 1.0. Sec. 3.3.5 has XGBoost eta 0.3, min_child_weight 0, lambda 1 and 100 estimators, with hinge, squared, unhinged and ramp losses. Table 1 lists 14 datasets. Nawaz's seven classifiers match sources/notes.md.

findings.text: The LR C sentence is inaccurate. It says the median C 'falls' on breast_cancer, credit-g and adult, but 'does not fall consistently' on covtype. On covtype the endpoints fall by a factor of about 3.6 (2.25 to 0.62). breast_cancer (0.0492 to 0.051) and adult (0.0195 to 0.0202) are not monotone either. What differs is the level: C stays near 1 on covtype, against 0.04 or less elsewhere at rho = 0.4.
findings.remedy: Rephrase in terms of level, or 'falls between the endpoints on all four; on covtype it stays an order of magnitude weaker'.
findings.ruling: Fixed. The endpoints match the macros: bc 0.276 -> 0.0428, cg 0.272 -> 0.00698, ad 0.38 -> 0.00584, ct 2.25 -> 0.62. Non-monotone paths are stated. 'Around an order of magnitude larger' understates it slightly: at rho=0.4 covtype's C is 14x to 106x the others. The direction is right.

findings.text: 'We add a protocol and an honest negative' calls an inconclusive result a negative one. 'Negative' reads as evidence of no difference, which the paper elsewhere says an inconclusive outcome is not.

findings.text: On covtype the paper says that 'the smallest meaningful difference is met'. Under the pre-specified rule this refers to the point estimate (|D| = 0.073 >= 0.05, drop difference >= 0.01), and the outcome 'supported' is correctly applied. But the interval [0.022, 0.124] reaches below the paper's own 0.05 threshold of a meaningful difference. The data therefore do not rule out a difference the paper itself would call not meaningful. The text never says so, and covtype is the only positive outcome in the paper.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex lines 413-419 (covtype bullet) and 550-552 (What the evidence supports); numbers.tex HOneDCt 0.073, HOneDCtLo 0.022, HOneDCtHi 0.124
findings.remedy: Add one clause: the point estimate meets the 0.05 threshold, but the interval's lower end (\HOneDCtLo) does not, so a difference smaller than 0.05 is not excluded.
findings.response: Covtype bullet and 'What the evidence supports' now say only the point estimate meets 0.05; the interval's lower end (\HOneDCtLo) is below it, so a smaller difference is not excluded.
